description:
FILED s520 (Fable, 2026-10-18 10:4x) from the USER's free `/code-review ultra` run on s519a (clone review/ultra-s519a; the review session's probed record: briefs-and-rules-for-claude-subagents/s520/ultrareview-s519a.md; probe programs ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/ultrareview-s519a-probes/).  Fable RE-RAN every probe (perl 5.40.3 / the pre-batch base fca3593b = review/base-fca3593b / merged main 02a35add = review/wt-main29) and the three-way table below is Fable's own.  s519a is MERGED (MAIN-READY-29): this is ON MAIN.  None of the shapes occurs in the gate, the sweep or everyday (which is why they passed).  The s519a guard file Pl/t/local-term-01.t is where the guard rows go (inverse-verified on an fd04c048 extraction = the shape FAILS there).

R1 + R8 of the ultra review (both are "what may PRECEDE the `local`").

R1 -- Pl/Parser2.pm `_split_void_local_list` (~6995-7013; the statement-shape test at ~6986) splits at EVERY top-level comma without checking that the comma is the statement's LOOSEST operator.  A paren-less list operator or call (print / return / push / die / `foo LIST`) or a looser `and` / `or` / `not` at the same level OWNS the list.
  f1:  our $x = 0; print "a", local $x = 5; print "\n";            perl a5   base a5   MAIN a      (the local became its own statement; print lost its second argument)
  f1b: our $x = 0; my $ok = 1; sub h { 2 }  $ok or h(), local $x = 9; print "x=$x\n";   perl x=0   base x=0   MAIN x=9   (the `or` short-circuit no longer guards the local: `$ok or h(); local $x = 9;`)
  `_logical_local_list` does not catch f1b because its first loop wants `local` right after the `or`; `_local_value_consumed`'s void test has the same gap.
  FIX SHAPE: before splitting, the statement's top level must have the comma as its loosest operator AND its first term must not be a list-operator / call word taking unparenthesised arguments; otherwise route to the refusal / announce (ruling 4), never split.  Probe the breaking cases: `return 1, local $x = 2` (perl returns the list), `push @l, local $x = 3`, `die "x", local $y`, `foo 1, local $x` with a declared `sub foo`, and the shapes that MUST still split (`$n++, local($g), $g = 2 if C`; Capture::Tiny's `$l{o}++, local(*STDOUT), _open(...) if COND`).

R8 -- Pl/Parser2.pm `_hoist_local_term` (~7100-7110): the safety scan before the `local` word skips every Word, every `(`/`)` structure and the operators `=` `->` `\`, so `foo()->m(local $x = 1)` / `$o->get->set(local $x = 1)` hoist although foo / get RUN BEFORE the term in perl.
  f8:  our $X = 'outer'; sub cfg { print "cfg sees ", defined $X ? $X : 'undef', "\n"; bless {}, 'C' } sub C::apply { }  cfg()->apply(local $X = 'new'); print "after: $X\n";
       perl: cfg sees outer / after: new    base: the same    MAIN: cfg sees UNDEF / after: new
  FIX SHAPE: the hoist invariant ("nothing evaluated earlier can observe the pre-local value") must be CHECKED, not assumed: reject the hoist when a Word followed by a call (an argument list, or a method name after `->`) precedes the `local`, except the call that directly owns the local's argument list (`f(local $x = 1)` stays hoistable: f runs AFTER its arguments).  Put the rejected shape through ruling 4 (announce in void, die in value position).

BAR: f1, f1b, f8 = perl; the s519a guard rows (local-term-01.t rows 1-14, moo-01.t 15/15, perl-tests/multideref.t 61) unchanged; corpus-diff vs fd04c048 (the split's 7 files) explained; the FULL SWEEP.


Related: #3370 (the lowering), #3414 (the announce residue), #3415 (nested-key local on the wrong slot), #3361 (data point 4: these sat on main; the instrument that found them was the cloud review, not a leg).  The fix batch: briefs-and-rules-for-claude-subagents/s520/s520b-prompt.md.


=== DONE (s520b) ===
m0 commit e74aa0a0 (+ row 28 a53d0178, ir-conform 136-local out of known-fail.tsv bd6acc60).  ONE question (rule 11): Parser2 `_word_before_local` -- a word before the term is inert / an OWNER (its arguments hold the term, it runs after) / FIRST (a call that runs before); `_word_takes_list` is its paren-less half (named unaries and term words excluded through PExpr::is_named_unary and `_word_is_term`).  SPLIT: refuses a list a loose and/or/xor/not owns and one with a paren-less list operator in any term but the last; `_logical_local_list` now takes `COND and/or LIST` with the local ANYWHERE at the right operand's top level (f1b lowers as `h(), local $x = 9 unless $ok`).  HOIST: a FIRST word refuses, except a method INVOCANT bound to a temporary before the local (`_local_invocant`: `cfg()->apply(local $X = 'new')` -> `my $__pcl_linv_N = cfg(); local $X; $__pcl_linv_N->apply($X = 'new');`); a comma is allowed only after an owner; literals / `!` inert (`_token_inert_before_local`); NEW: a term in an assignment's LEFT operand checks the right side too (fd04c048 hoisted `(local $g) = ($g + 1)` above its right side: in g=1, perl 2 -- now announced, appended to #3414).  Probes perl / fd04c048 / tree: f1 a5,x=9 / a,x=9 / a5,x=9; f1b x=0 / x=9 / x=0; f8 `cfg sees outer` / `cfg sees undef` / `cfg sees outer`; return / push / die / declared foo LIST all = perl (row 17).  Guards Pl/t/local-term-01.t rows 17-21 (FAIL on fd04c048).  Kept: rows 1-16, moo-01.t 15/15, multideref.t (corpus IDENTICAL; :215 `@{local $x[0][0]} = 1` still hoists, :220 still refuses).
